passages.text: By now Abraham was old and well along in years, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.
passages.sermon: Abraham was old.\r\nHe had lived many years.\r\nThe LORD had blessed Abraham in every way.
passages.original: וְאַבְרָהָ֣ם זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַֽיהוָ֛ה בֵּרַ֥ךְ אֶת־ אַבְרָהָ֖ם בַּכֹּֽל׃

passages.text: So Abraham instructed the chief servant of his household, who managed all he owned, “Place your hand under my thigh, and I will have you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I am dwelling, but will go to my country and my kindred to take a wife for my son Isaac.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was old.
The LORD had blessed Abraham in every way.
Abraham had a chief servant.
This servant managed everything Abraham owned.
Abraham spoke to his servant.
Abraham said, “Put your hand under my thigh.”
Abraham said, “I want you to make a promise.”
Abraham said, “Swear by the LORD.”
The LORD is the God of heaven and the God of earth.
Abraham said, “Do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites.”
Abraham lived among the Canaanites.
Abraham said, “Go to my country.”
Abraham said, “Go to my family.”
Abraham said, “Take a wife for my son Isaac from there.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶל־ עַבְדּוֹ֙ זְקַ֣ן בֵּית֔וֹ הַמֹּשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֑וֹ שִֽׂים־ נָ֥א יָדְךָ֖ תַּ֥חַת יְרֵכִֽי׃ וְאַשְׁבִּ֣יעֲךָ֔ בַּֽיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃ כִּ֧י אֶל־ אַרְצִ֛י וְאֶל־ מוֹלַדְתִּ֖י תֵּלֵ֑ךְ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֖ה לִבְנִ֥י לְיִצְחָֽק׃

passages.text: The servant asked him, “What if the woman is unwilling to follow me to this land? Shall I then take your son back to the land from which you came?”
passages.sermon:
Abraham had a chief servant.
This servant managed everything Abraham owned.
Abraham told the servant to find a wife for his son Isaac.
Abraham did not want a wife for Isaac from the Canaanites.
Abraham wanted a wife for Isaac from his own country and family.
The servant spoke to Abraham.
The servant asked a question.
He said, “What if the woman will not come with me to this land?”
He asked, “Should I take your son back to the land you came from?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הָעֶ֔בֶד אוּלַי֙ לֹא־ תֹאבֶ֣ה הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה לָלֶ֥כֶת אַחֲרַ֖י אֶל־ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את הֶֽהָשֵׁ֤ב אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת־ בִּנְךָ֔ אֶל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ יָצָ֥אתָ מִשָּֽׁם׃

passages.text: Abraham replied, “Make sure that you do not take my son back there.
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to his servant.
Abraham gave a warning.
Abraham said, “Be careful.”
Abraham said, “Do not take my son back there.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו אַבְרָהָ֑ם הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֔ פֶּן־ תָּשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ בְּנִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: The LORD, the God of heaven, who brought me from my father’s house and my native land, who spoke to me and promised me on oath, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give this land’—He will send His angel before you so that you can take a wife for my son from there.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of heaven.
He brought me out of my father’s house.
He brought me out of my native land.
He spoke to me.
He promised me with an oath.
He said, “I will give this land to your offspring.”
He will send His angel ahead of you.
You will take a wife for my son from there.
passages.original: יְהוָ֣ה׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לְקָחַ֜נִי מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִי֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ מֽוֹלַדְתִּי֒ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּר־ לִ֜י וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִֽשְׁבַּֽע־ לִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַ֨רְעֲךָ֔ אֶתֵּ֖ן אֶת־ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את ה֗וּא יִשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכוֹ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֛ה לִבְנִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃

passages.text: And if the woman is unwilling to follow you, then you are released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to his servant.
Abraham gave a command about his son Isaac.
Abraham said, “If the woman does not want to come with you, you are free from my oath.
You do not have to bring her if she refuses.
But do not take my son Isaac back there.”
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֨א תֹאבֶ֤ה הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ וְנִקִּ֕יתָ מִשְּׁבֻעָתִ֖י זֹ֑את רַ֣ק אֶת־ בְּנִ֔י לֹ֥א תָשֵׁ֖ב שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore an oath to him concerning this matter.
passages.sermon: Abraham was the servant’s master.\r\nThe servant placed his hand under Abraham’s thigh.\r\nThe servant swore an oath to Abraham about this matter.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם הָעֶ֙בֶד֙ אֶת־ יָד֔וֹ תַּ֛חַת יֶ֥רֶךְ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׁ֣בַֽע ל֔וֹ עַל־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed with all manner of good things from his master in hand. And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was the master of the servant.
The servant took ten camels from Abraham.
The servant gathered many valuable things from Abraham.
The servant held these good things in his hand.
The servant stood up.
The servant left on his journey.
The servant traveled to Aram-naharaim.
The servant went to the city of Nahor.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח הָ֠עֶבֶד עֲשָׂרָ֨ה גְמַלִּ֜ים מִגְּמַלֵּ֤י אֲדֹנָיו֙ וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל־ ט֥וּב אֲדֹנָ֖יו בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֗קָם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ אֲרַ֥ם נַֽהֲרַ֖יִם אֶל־ עִ֥יר נָחֽוֹר׃

passages.text: As evening approached, he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town at the time when the women went out to draw water.
passages.sermon:
Abraham had a servant.
The servant traveled with camels.
He reached a town.
He stopped outside the town.
There was a well of water outside the town.
It was evening.
The servant made the camels kneel down near the well.
At that time, women from the town went out to draw water.
passages.original: וַיַּבְרֵ֧ךְ הַגְּמַלִּ֛ים מִח֥וּץ לָעִ֖יר אֶל־ בְּאֵ֣ר הַמָּ֑יִם לְעֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב לְעֵ֖ת צֵ֥את הַשֹּׁאֲבֹֽת׃

passages.text: “O LORD, God of my master Abraham,” he prayed, “please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
passages.sermon:
The servant prayed to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Abraham.
Abraham is the servant’s master.
The servant asked the LORD for success that day.
The servant asked the LORD to show kindness to Abraham.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֓ר׀ יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם הַקְרֵה־ נָ֥א לְפָנַ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וַעֲשֵׂה־ חֶ֕סֶד עִ֖ם אֲדֹנִ֥י אַבְרָהָֽם׃

passages.text: Here I am, standing beside the spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water.
passages.sermon:
The servant of Abraham stood beside the spring.
He was outside the town.
The daughters of the townspeople came out to draw water.
They walked to the spring.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב עַל־ עֵ֣ין הַמָּ֑יִם וּבְנוֹת֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֔יר יֹצְאֹ֖ת לִשְׁאֹ֥ב מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Now may it happen that the girl to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and who responds, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. By this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham’s servant prayed to the Lord.
He asked God for a sign.
He said, “I will speak to a young woman at the spring.”
He planned to say, “Please lower your jar so I may drink.”
He looked for a girl who would answer, “Drink, and I will also give water to your camels.”
He asked God to choose this girl for Isaac, Abraham’s son.
He said, “By this sign, I will know You have shown kindness to my master Abraham.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֹמַ֤ר אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ הַטִּי־ נָ֤א כַדֵּךְ֙ וְאֶשְׁתֶּ֔ה וְאָמְרָ֣ה שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַם־ גְּמַלֶּ֖יךָ אַשְׁקֶ֑ה אֹתָ֤הּ הֹכַ֙חְתָּ֙ לְעַבְדְּךָ֣ לְיִצְחָ֔ק וּבָ֣הּ אֵדַ֔ע כִּי־ עָשִׂ֥יתָ חֶ֖סֶד עִם־ אֲדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor.
passages.sermon:
The servant prayed at the spring.
Before he finished praying, Rebekah came out.
Rebekah carried her jar on her shoulder.
Rebekah was the daughter of Bethuel.
Bethuel was the son of Milcah.
Milcah was the wife of Nahor.
Nahor was Abraham’s brother.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי־ ה֗וּא טֶרֶם֮ כִּלָּ֣ה לְדַבֵּר֒ וְהִנֵּ֧ה רִבְקָ֣ה יֹצֵ֗את אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֻלְּדָה֙ לִבְתוּאֵ֣ל בֶּן־ מִלְכָּ֔ה אֵ֥שֶׁת נָח֖וֹר אֲחִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וְכַדָּ֖הּ עַל־ שִׁכְמָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Now the girl was very beautiful, a virgin who had not had relations with any man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up again.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was a young woman.
She was very beautiful.
She was a virgin.
No man had known her.
She went down to the spring.
She filled her jar with water.
She came up from the spring.
passages.original: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ טֹבַ֤ת מַרְאֶה֙ מְאֹ֔ד בְּתוּלָ֕ה וְאִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א יְדָעָ֑הּ וַתֵּ֣רֶד הָעַ֔יְנָה וַתְּמַלֵּ֥א כַדָּ֖הּ וַתָּֽעַל׃

passages.text: So the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me have a little water from your jar.”
passages.sermon:
The servant saw Rebekah.
He ran to meet her.
He spoke to her.
He said, “Please give me a little water from your jar.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֥רָץ הָעֶ֖בֶד לִקְרָאתָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הַגְמִיאִ֥ינִי נָ֛א מְעַט־ מַ֖יִם מִכַּדֵּֽךְ׃

passages.text: “Drink, my lord,” she replied, and she quickly lowered her jar to her hands and gave him a drink.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was a very beautiful young woman.
She was a virgin.
No man had known her.
She went down to the spring.
She filled her jar.
She came up again.
Abraham’s servant ran to meet her.
He said, “Please let me have a little water from your jar.”
Rebekah replied, “Drink, my lord.”
She quickly lowered her jar to her hands.
She gave him a drink.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שְׁתֵ֣ה אֲדֹנִ֑י וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתֹּ֧רֶד כַּדָּ֛הּ עַל־ יָדָ֖הּ וַתַּשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: After she had given him a drink, she said, “I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah finished giving the servant a drink.
She spoke to the servant.
She said she would draw water for his camels.
She said she would keep drawing water until the camels finished drinking.
passages.original: וַתְּכַ֖ל לְהַשְׁקֹת֑וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר גַּ֤ם לִגְמַלֶּ֙יךָ֙ אֶשְׁאָ֔ב עַ֥ד אִם־ כִּלּ֖וּ לִשְׁתֹּֽת׃

passages.text: And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw water, until she had drawn water for all his camels.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah acted quickly.
She poured her jar of water into the trough.
She ran again to the well.
She drew more water.
She continued until she had given water to all his camels.
passages.original: וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתְּעַ֤ר כַּדָּהּ֙ אֶל־ הַשֹּׁ֔קֶת וַתָּ֥רָץ ע֛וֹד אֶֽל־ הַבְּאֵ֖ר לִשְׁאֹ֑ב וַתִּשְׁאַ֖ב לְכָל־ גְּמַלָּֽיו׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, the man watched her silently to see whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.
passages.sermon:
The man stood nearby.
He watched the woman.
He did not speak.
He wanted to know something.
He wanted to see if the LORD had made his journey successful.
He waited to find out if God had helped him or not.
passages.original: וְהָאִ֥ישׁ מִשְׁתָּאֵ֖ה לָ֑הּ מַחֲרִ֕ישׁ לָדַ֗עַת הַֽהִצְלִ֧יחַ יְהוָ֛ה דַּרְכּ֖וֹ אִם־ לֹֽא׃

passages.text: And after the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring weighing a beka, and two gold bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels.
passages.sermon:
The man watched the camels.
The camels finished drinking.
The man acted next.
He took a gold ring.
The gold ring weighed a beka.
He also took two gold bracelets.
The bracelets were for her wrists.
The bracelets weighed ten shekels of gold.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר כִּלּ֤וּ הַגְּמַלִּים֙ לִשְׁתּ֔וֹת וַיִּקַּ֤ח הָאִישׁ֙ נֶ֣זֶם זָהָ֔ב בֶּ֖קַע מִשְׁקָל֑וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֤י צְמִידִים֙ עַל־ יָדֶ֔יהָ עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מִשְׁקָלָֽם׃

passages.text: “Whose daughter are you?” he asked. “Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?”
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to a young woman at a well.
He asked her a question.
He said, "Whose daughter are you?"
He wanted to know her family.
He also asked another question.
He said, "Please tell me, is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"
He wanted to know if they could stay at her home.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ בַּת־ מִ֣י אַ֔תְּ הַגִּ֥ידִי נָ֖א לִ֑י הֲיֵ֧שׁ בֵּית־ אָבִ֛יךְ מָק֥וֹם לָ֖נוּ לָלִֽין׃

passages.text: She replied, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor.”
passages.sermon:
A young woman spoke to the man.
She said, “I am Bethuel’s daughter.”
Bethuel is the son of Milcah.
Milcah gave birth to Bethuel for Nahor.
Nahor is my grandfather.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו בַּת־ בְּתוּאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי בֶּן־ מִלְכָּ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֖ה לְנָחֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Then she added, “We have plenty of straw and feed, as well as a place for you to spend the night.”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah spoke to the man.
She said, "We have plenty of straw."
She said, "We have plenty of feed."
She said, "We also have a place for you to spend the night."
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו גַּם־ תֶּ֥בֶן גַּם־ מִסְפּ֖וֹא רַ֣ב עִמָּ֑נוּ גַּם־ מָק֖וֹם לָלֽוּן׃

passages.text: Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD, saying, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives.”
passages.sermon:
A man stood by the spring.
This man served Abraham.
He bowed down.
He worshiped the LORD.
He spoke.
He said, “Blessed be the LORD.
The LORD is the God of my master Abraham.
The LORD has not withheld kindness from my master.
The LORD has not withheld faithfulness from my master.
The LORD has led me on my journey.
The LORD has brought me to the house of my master’s relatives.”
passages.original: וַיִּקֹּ֣ד הָאִ֔ישׁ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַֽיהוָֽה׃ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ עָזַ֥ב חַסְדּ֛וֹ וַאֲמִתּ֖וֹ מֵעִ֣ם אֲדֹנִ֑י אָנֹכִ֗י בַּדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ נָחַ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אֲחֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: The girl ran and told her mother’s household about these things.
passages.sermon:
A girl named Rebekah saw what happened at the spring.
Rebekah ran quickly.
She went to her mother’s household.
Rebekah told her mother’s household about these things.
passages.original: וַתָּ֙רָץ֙ הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ וַתַּגֵּ֖ד לְבֵ֣ית אִמָּ֑הּ כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he rushed out to the man at the spring.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah had a brother.
His name was Laban.
Laban saw a man at the spring.
Laban ran out to meet the man.
passages.original: וּלְרִבְקָ֥ה אָ֖ח וּשְׁמ֣וֹ לָבָ֑ן וַיָּ֨רָץ לָבָ֧ן אֶל־ הָאִ֛ישׁ הַח֖וּצָה אֶל־ הָעָֽיִן׃

passages.text: As soon as he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and heard Rebekah’s words, “The man said this to me,” he went and found the man standing by the camels near the spring.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Rebekah’s brother.
Laban saw a ring on his sister’s nose.
He saw bracelets on her wrists.
He listened to Rebekah’s words.
Rebekah said, “The man said this to me.”
Laban went to find the man.
He saw the man standing by the camels.
The man was near the spring.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ כִּרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־ הַנֶּ֗זֶם וְֽאֶת־ הַצְּמִדִים֮ עַל־ יְדֵ֣י אֲחֹתוֹ֒ וּכְשָׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֞י רִבְקָ֤ה אֲחֹתוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה־ דִבֶּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־ הָאִ֔ישׁ וְהִנֵּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־ הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים עַל־ הָעָֽיִן׃

passages.text: “Come, you who are blessed by the LORD,” said Laban. “Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to the man.
Laban said, “Come inside.
You are blessed by the LORD.
Why are you standing outside?
I have made the house ready for you.
I have also prepared a place for the camels.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בּ֖וֹא בְּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה לָ֤מָּה תַעֲמֹד֙ בַּח֔וּץ וְאָנֹכִי֙ פִּנִּ֣יתִי הַבַּ֔יִת וּמָק֖וֹם לַגְּמַלִּֽים׃

passages.text: So the man came to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and feed were brought to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of his companions.
passages.sermon:
The man entered the house.
He unloaded the camels.
He brought straw and feed for the camels.
He brought water to wash his feet.
He brought water to wash the feet of the men who were with him.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָאִישׁ֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַיְפַתַּ֖ח הַגְּמַלִּ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֨ן תֶּ֤בֶן וּמִסְפּוֹא֙ לַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וּמַ֙יִם֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ רַגְלָ֔יו וְרַגְלֵ֥י הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then a meal was set before the man, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told you what I came to say.” So Laban said, “Please speak.”
passages.sermon:
They set food in front of the man.
The man was Abraham’s servant.
He said, “I will not eat.”
He said, “I must speak my words first.”
Laban said, “Speak.”
passages.original: וַיִּישֶׂם לְפָנָיו֙ לֶאֱכֹ֔ל וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֹכַ֔ל עַ֥ד אִם־ דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי דְּבָרָ֑י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: “I am Abraham’s servant,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
I am a servant.
I serve Abraham.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: “The LORD has greatly blessed my master, and he has become rich. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, menservants and maidservants, camels and donkeys.
passages.sermon:
The LORD has blessed my master.
My master is Abraham.
The LORD has blessed Abraham very much.
Abraham has become rich.
The LORD has given Abraham sheep.
The LORD has given Abraham cattle.
The LORD has given Abraham silver.
The LORD has given Abraham gold.
The LORD has given Abraham male servants.
The LORD has given Abraham female servants.
The LORD has given Abraham camels.
The LORD has given Abraham donkeys.
passages.original: וַיהוָ֞ה בֵּרַ֧ךְ אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֛י מְאֹ֖ד וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֞וֹ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וְכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וַעֲבָדִם֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: My master’s wife Sarah has borne him a son in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns.
passages.sermon:
Sarah is my master’s wife.
Sarah gave birth to a son for my master.
Sarah was old when she gave birth to this son.
My master gave everything he owns to this son.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֡לֶד שָׂרָה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת אֲדֹנִ֥י בֵן֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י אַחֲרֵ֖י זִקְנָתָ֑הּ וַיִּתֶּן־ לּ֖וֹ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: My master made me swear an oath and said, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I dwell, but you shall go to my father’s house and to my kindred to take a wife for my son.’
passages.sermon:
Abraham is my master.
Abraham lives in the land of the Canaanites.
Abraham made me swear an oath.
He said, “Do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites.”
He said, “Go to my father’s house.”
He said, “Go to my family.”
He said, “Take a wife for my son from there.”
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁבִּעֵ֥נִי אֲדֹנִ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹא־ תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃ אִם־ לֹ֧א אֶל־ בֵּית־ אָבִ֛י תֵּלֵ֖ךְ וְאֶל־ מִשְׁפַּחְתִּ֑י וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֖ה לִבְנִֽי׃

passages.text: Then I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not come back with me?’
passages.sermon: I spoke to my master Abraham.\r\nI said, "Perhaps the woman will not follow me."\r\nI asked, "What if she will not come back with me?"
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֑י אֻלַ֛י לֹא־ תֵלֵ֥ךְ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אַחֲרָֽי׃

passages.text: And he told me, ‘The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you may take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father’s house.
passages.sermon:
Abraham is my master.
Abraham has walked faithfully before the LORD.
Abraham spoke to me.
He said, "The LORD will send His angel with you."
The LORD will make your journey successful.
You will take a wife for my master's son.
You will choose her from my master's family.
You will find her in my master's father's house.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י יְהוָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנָ֗יו יִשְׁלַ֨ח מַלְאָכ֤וֹ אִתָּךְ֙ וְהִצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתִּ֖י וּמִבֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: And when you go to my kindred, if they refuse to give her to you, then you will be released from my oath.’
passages.sermon:
Abraham was my master.
Abraham gave me an oath.
He told me to find a wife for his son from his family.
He said, "When you go to my family, you must ask them."
If my family does not give you the woman, you are free from my oath.
You will not be bound by my promise if they refuse.
passages.original: אָ֤ז תִּנָּקֶה֙ מֵאָ֣לָתִ֔י כִּ֥י תָב֖וֹא אֶל־ מִשְׁפַּחְתִּ֑י וְאִם־ לֹ֤א יִתְּנוּ֙ לָ֔ךְ וְהָיִ֥יתָ נָקִ֖י מֵאָלָתִֽי׃

passages.text: So when I came to the spring today, I prayed: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if only You would make my journey a success!
passages.sermon:
I came to the spring today.
I prayed at the spring.
I spoke to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of my master Abraham.
I asked the LORD to make my journey successful.
I am walking on this journey now.
passages.original: וָאָבֹ֥א הַיּ֖וֹם אֶל־ הָעָ֑יִן וָאֹמַ֗ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אִם־ יֶשְׁךָ־ נָּא֙ מַצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכִּ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י הֹלֵ֥ךְ עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Here I am, standing beside this spring. Now if a maiden comes out to draw water and I say to her, ‘Please let me drink a little water from your jar,’ and she replies, ‘Drink, and I will draw water for your camels as well,’ may she be the woman the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.
passages.sermon:
I am standing beside the spring.
A young woman comes out to draw water.
I say to her, "Please let me drink a little water from your jar."
She answers, "Drink, and I will also draw water for your camels."
She is the woman the LORD has chosen for my master's son.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב עַל־ עֵ֣ין הַמָּ֑יִם וְהָיָ֤ה הָֽעַלְמָה֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣את לִשְׁאֹ֔ב וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י אֵלֶ֔יהָ הַשְׁקִֽינִי־ נָ֥א מְעַט־ מַ֖יִם מִכַּדֵּֽךְ׃ וְאָמְרָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ גַּם־ אַתָּ֣ה שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַ֥ם לִגְמַלֶּ֖יךָ אֶשְׁאָ֑ב הִ֣וא הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ הֹכִ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה לְבֶן־ אֲדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: And before I had finished praying in my heart, there was Rebekah coming out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. So I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’
passages.sermon:
I had not finished praying in my heart.
Rebekah came out.
She carried her jar on her shoulder.
She went down to the spring.
She drew water.
I spoke to her.
I said, "Please give me a drink."
passages.original: אֲנִי֩ טֶ֨רֶם אֲכַלֶּ֜ה לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ לִבִּ֗י וְהִנֵּ֨ה רִבְקָ֤ה יֹצֵאת֙ וְכַדָּ֣הּ עַל־ שִׁכְמָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֥רֶד הָעַ֖יְנָה וַתִּשְׁאָ֑ב וָאֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ הַשְׁקִ֥ינִי נָֽא׃

passages.text: She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well.’ So I drank, and she also watered the camels.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah saw me at the spring.
She acted quickly.
She took her jar down from her shoulder.
She spoke to me.
She said, "Drink."
She also said, "I will give water to your camels."
I drank the water she gave me.
She gave water to my camels too.
passages.original: וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתּ֤וֹרֶד כַּדָּהּ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַם־ גְּמַלֶּ֖יךָ אַשְׁקֶ֑ה וָאֵ֕שְׁתְּ וְגַ֥ם הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים הִשְׁקָֽתָה׃

passages.text: Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She replied, ‘The daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.’ So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.
passages.sermon:
I spoke to the young woman named Rebekah.
I asked her, "Whose daughter are you?"
She answered me.
She said, "I am the daughter of Bethuel."
Bethuel is the son of Nahor.
Milcah gave birth to Bethuel.
I took a ring.
I placed the ring on her nose.
I took bracelets.
I put the bracelets on her wrists.
passages.original: וָאֶשְׁאַ֣ל אֹתָ֗הּ וָאֹמַר֮ בַּת־ מִ֣י אַתְּ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בַּת־ בְּתוּאֵל֙ בֶּן־ נָח֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָֽלְדָה־ לּ֖וֹ מִלְכָּ֑ה וָאָשִׂ֤ם הַנֶּ֙זֶם֙ עַל־ אַפָּ֔הּ וְהַצְּמִידִ֖ים עַל־ יָדֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Then I bowed down and worshiped the LORD; and I blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to take the granddaughter of my master’s brother for his son.
passages.sermon:
I am Abraham’s servant.
Abraham is my master.
The LORD is the God of my master Abraham.
I bowed down before the LORD.
I worshiped the LORD.
I blessed the LORD.
The LORD led me on the right road.
The LORD guided me faithfully.
The LORD helped me find the granddaughter of my master’s brother.
I took her for my master’s son.
passages.original: וָאֶקֹּ֥ד וָֽאֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה וָאֲבָרֵ֗ךְ אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִנְחַ֙נִי֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֱמֶ֔ת לָקַ֛חַת אֶת־ בַּת־ אֲחִ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י לִבְנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; but if not, let me know, so that I may go elsewhere.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham had a servant.
The servant spoke to Rebekah’s family.
He said, “If you will show kindness to my master, tell me.”
He said, “If you will show faithfulness to my master, tell me.”
He said, “If you will not, tell me.”
He said, “Then I will go another way.”
passages.original: וְ֠עַתָּה אִם־ יֶשְׁכֶ֨ם עֹשִׂ֜ים חֶ֧סֶד וֶֽאֱמֶ֛ת אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֑י וְאִם־ לֹ֕א הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֔י וְאֶפְנֶ֥ה עַל־ יָמִ֖ין א֥וֹ עַל־ שְׂמֹֽאל׃

passages.text: Laban and Bethuel answered, “This is from the LORD; we have no choice in the matter.
passages.sermon:
Laban and Bethuel spoke.
They answered Abraham’s servant.
They said, “This matter comes from the LORD.
We cannot say anything to you.
We cannot say bad or good.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן לָבָ֤ן וּבְתוּאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵיְהוָ֖ה יָצָ֣א הַדָּבָ֑ר לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רַ֥ע אוֹ־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: Rebekah is here before you. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, just as the LORD has decreed.”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah stands here in front of you.
You may take her now.
Go with her.
Let Rebekah become the wife of your master’s son.
The LORD has spoken this.
This is what the LORD has decided.
passages.original: הִנֵּֽה־ רִבְקָ֥ה לְפָנֶ֖יךָ קַ֣ח וָלֵ֑ךְ וּתְהִ֤י אִשָּׁה֙ לְבֶן־ אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Abraham had a servant.
The servant listened to the words of Laban and Bethuel.
He heard what they said.
He bowed down to the ground.
He worshiped the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֛ע עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־ דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַ֖רְצָה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and he gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother.
passages.sermon:
Abraham’s servant stood there.
He took out silver jewelry.
He took out gold jewelry.
He took out clothing.
He gave these gifts to Rebekah.
He also gave precious gifts to Rebekah’s brother.
He also gave precious gifts to Rebekah’s mother.
passages.original: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א הָעֶ֜בֶד כְּלֵי־ כֶ֨סֶף וּכְלֵ֤י זָהָב֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לְרִבְקָ֑ה וּמִ֨גְדָּנֹ֔ת נָתַ֥ן לְאָחִ֖יהָ וּלְאִמָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then he and the men with him ate and drank and spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, he said, “Send me on my way to my master.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham’s servant was traveling with other men.
They ate together.
They drank together.
They spent the night there.
In the morning, they got up.
Abraham’s servant spoke.
He said, “Send me on my way to my master.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֗וּ ה֛וּא וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ עִמּ֖וֹ וַיָּלִ֑ינוּ וַיָּק֣וּמוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שַׁלְּחֻ֥נִי לַֽאדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: But her brother and mother said, “Let the girl remain with us ten days or so. After that, she may go.”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah had a brother and a mother.
They spoke to the servant.
They said, “Let the girl stay with us for a few days.
Let her stay for ten days or so.
After that, she can go.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָחִ֙יהָ֙ וְאִמָּ֔הּ תֵּשֵׁ֨ב הַנַּעֲרָ֥ אִתָּ֛נוּ יָמִ֖ים א֣וֹ עָשׂ֑וֹר אַחַ֖ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: But he replied, “Do not delay me, since the LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so that I may go to my master.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham’s servant spoke to Rebekah’s family.
He said, “Do not delay me.”
The LORD has made my journey successful.
Send me on my way.
I must go to my master.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַל־ תְּאַחֲר֣וּ אֹתִ֔י וַֽיהוָ֖ה הִצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכִּ֑י שַׁלְּח֕וּנִי וְאֵלְכָ֖ה לַֽאדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: So they said, “We will call the girl and ask her opinion.”
passages.sermon: Rebekah’s family spoke together.\r\nThey said, “We will call the girl.”\r\nThey said, “We will ask her what she wants.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ נִקְרָ֣א לַֽנַּעֲרָ֑ וְנִשְׁאֲלָ֖ה אֶת־ פִּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: They called Rebekah and asked her, “Will you go with this man?” “I will go,” she replied.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was the sister in this family.
They called Rebekah.
They spoke to her.
They asked her a question.
They said, "Will you go with this man?"
Rebekah answered them.
She said, "I will go."
passages.original: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ לְרִבְקָה֙ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ הֲתֵלְכִ֖י עִם־ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וַתֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was their sister.
They sent Rebekah away.
They sent her nurse with her.
They sent Abraham’s servant with her.
They sent the servant’s men with her.
passages.original: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת־ רִבְקָ֥ה אֲחֹתָ֖ם וְאֶת־ מֵנִקְתָּ֑הּ וְאֶת־ עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְאֶת־ אֲנָשָֽׁיו׃

passages.text: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah’s family spoke to her.
They blessed Rebekah.
They said, “You are our sister.
May you become the mother of many thousands.
May your children take the gates of their enemies.”
passages.original: וַיְבָרֲכ֤וּ אֶת־ רִבְקָה֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לָ֔הּ אֲחֹתֵ֕נוּ אַ֥תְּ הֲיִ֖י לְאַלְפֵ֣י רְבָבָ֑ה וְיִירַ֣שׁ זַרְעֵ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת שַׁ֥עַר שֹׂנְאָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah stood up.
Her servant girls stood up with her.
They all got ready.
They climbed onto the camels.
They followed the man.
The man was Abraham’s servant.
The servant took Rebekah.
He left with her.
passages.original: וַתָּ֨קָם רִבְקָ֜ה וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֗יהָ וַתִּרְכַּ֙בְנָה֙ עַל־ הַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וַתֵּלַ֖כְנָה אַחֲרֵ֣י הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיִּקַּ֥ח הָעֶ֛בֶד אֶת־ רִבְקָ֖ה וַיֵּלַֽךְ׃

passages.text: Now Isaac had just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, for he was living in the Negev.
passages.sermon: Isaac was living in the Negev.\r\nIsaac returned from Beer-lahai-roi.
passages.original: וְיִצְחָק֙ בָּ֣א מִבּ֔וֹא בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י וְה֥וּא יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַנֶּֽגֶב׃

passages.text: Early in the evening, Isaac went out to the field to meditate, and looking up, he saw the camels approaching.
passages.sermon:
Isaac lived in the Negev.
Isaac went out to the field in the evening.
Isaac wanted to meditate.
Isaac looked up.
Isaac saw camels coming.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק לָשׂ֥וּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִפְנ֣וֹת עָ֑רֶב וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה גְמַלִּ֖ים בָּאִֽים׃

passages.text: And when Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she got down from her camel and asked the servant, “Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?” “It is my master,” the servant answered. So she took her veil and covered herself.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah traveled with Abraham’s servant to meet Isaac.
Rebekah looked up.
She saw Isaac.
Rebekah got down from her camel.
She spoke to the servant.
She asked, “Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?”
The servant answered her.
He said, “He is my master.”
Rebekah took her veil.
She covered herself with the veil.
passages.original: וַתִּשָּׂ֤א רִבְקָה֙ אֶת־ עֵינֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֖רֶא אֶת־ יִצְחָ֑ק וַתִּפֹּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל הַגָּמָֽל׃ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ הָעֶ֗בֶד מִֽי־ הָאִ֤ישׁ הַלָּזֶה֙ הַהֹלֵ֤ךְ בַּשָּׂדֶה֙ לִקְרָאתֵ֔נוּ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הָעֶ֖בֶד ה֣וּא אֲדֹנִ֑י וַתִּקַּ֥ח הַצָּעִ֖יף וַתִּתְכָּֽס׃

passages.text: Then the servant told Isaac all that he had done.
passages.sermon: The servant spoke to Isaac.\r\nThe servant told Isaac everything he had done.
passages.original: וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר הָעֶ֖בֶד לְיִצְחָ֑ק אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: And Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah and took Rebekah as his wife. And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the son of Abraham and Sarah.
Sarah was Isaac’s mother.
Sarah had died.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent that had belonged to his mother Sarah.
Isaac took Rebekah as his wife.
Isaac loved Rebekah.
Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.
passages.original: וַיְבִאֶ֣הָ יִצְחָ֗ק הָאֹ֙הֱלָה֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֧ח אֶת־ רִבְקָ֛ה וַתְּהִי־ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וַיֶּאֱהָבֶ֑הָ וַיִּנָּחֵ֥ם יִצְחָ֖ק אַחֲרֵ֥י אִמּֽוֹ׃פ
